contexts.text: The seed is then among thickets...
Among the thick boughs () = among scientifics. AE 388:12. AE 654:35.
To give the branch among the thick boughs () = to stick among scientifics, and to look thence at spiritual, celestial, and Divine things.
To reason from scientifics, is to give the branch among the thick boughs ().
The tangled tree () = those things which are not dictated by the Word, but by the scientific proprium.
The thickets of the forest () = scientifics.
Her clothing is of entwined things of gold () = the quality of that truth from good... What is entwined is predicated of the scientific Natural; here, of Divine truth natural. AC 5954:7. AE 863:14.
Therefore, also, scientifics are signified by the thickets of trees, and of the forest.
Under a tangled oak () = from falsities, which are the lowest things of the Natural; for these are in a tangle.
Scientifics from sensuous things are the tangled branches ().
The branch of a dense or tangled tree () = external truths of good, or scientifics.
In the Original Language there is meant a cord which is made of twisted and entwined work... That which is entwisted = what is scientific.
Plaited work () = scientific truth, which is exterior truth, or the truth of the external man. AC 10540:4.
Baldness in place of plaited work () = foolishness in place of knowledge.
